items.title: MACC submits several governance improvement recommendations to Felda, two subsidiaries
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has submitted several governance improvement recommendations to the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and two of its subsidiaries to enhance transparency in the implementation of the Agro Park (Commercial) Project and the Cattle Trading Pilot Project. MACC said that these recommendations were presented through its Governance Investigation Division to Felda, FIC Supplies Sdn Bhd, and FIC Integrated Property Management (FIC IPM). According to MACC, agreement on these recommendations was finalised through a Governance Improvement Report signed by Felda deputy director-general of Services Muhammad Fitri Othman, FIC Group chief executive officer Syed Fadil Syed Sofi, and MACC Governance Investigation Division Director Datuk Mohazaki Hassan.

items.title: IHH says Fortis stake acquired via transparent, widely public competitive bidding
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare Bhd said its position remained that its subsidiary, Northern TK Venture Pte Ltd (NTK), acquired its stake in Fortis Healthcare in 2018 through a transparent, widely public and fully regulated competitive bidding process. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the healthcare group said the transaction obtained all necessary corporate, shareholder and regulatory approvals, including those required under the Competition Commission of India (CCI) and the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) takeover regulations. "IHH's investment was made through a preferential allotment of newly issued Fortis shares amounting to INR4,000 crore for a 31 per cent stake, together with a mandatory tender offer to the public shareholders.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 28, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended lower on Monday, with the benchmark index falling 0.10 per cent, or 1.60 points, to 1,670. Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources and Evocom were among the most actively traded counters at the closing bell. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin is trading lower at RM338,398, while Ethereum also trended lower at RM10,822.

items.title: 'Maha' for Mahathir, Hasmah: Alor Setar clinic stands as lasting tribute to late couple
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Maha Klinik, a fixture here since 1957, stands as a testament to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad's enduring love for his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali. To this day, it remains associated with the names of Tun Dr Mahathir and Tun Dr Siti Hasmah. The late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah was always by Tun Dr Mahathir's side, wherever he went," she said.

items.title: Special delivery: India state hands out gold for newborns
items.summary: MADURAI: Authorities in India's Tamil Nadu state gave babies born in government-run hospitals a free gold ring on Monday, an initiative aimed at boosting confidence in the public healthcare system. Under the scheme launched by actor-turned-Chief Minister Vijay, all babies born in public health facilities in the state are eligible for a one-gram gold ring, worth some US$143. Gold has immense cultural significance in India, featuring prominently in weddings and religious ceremonies, and is seen as a safe generational asset.

items.title: Perak seeks RM1.4b in Budget 2027 for key water infrastructure
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 28 — Perak is hoping for at least RM1.4 billion in the upcoming Federal Budget to fund key water supply infrastructure, particularly a project to transfer water from Sungai Perak to Bukit Merah to support farmers regularly affected by drought. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the project was among the state’s priorities submitted by the Perak Economic Planning Unit to the Finance Ministry ahead of the Budget announcement. He said the project would involve two main components, with the first involving infrastructure such as pumps and water tunnels.

items.title: Federal Court allows Pelorus to directly recover RM2.4mil from former partners
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court has ruled that a joint venture partner can directly sue its former business partners to recover money it claims had been misused or diverted. The court held that Pelorus was entitled to enforce obligations owed directly to it under a joint venture agreement (JVA). Wan Ahmad Farid said the joint venture company, Pelorus HLG Sdn Bhd, had already been incorporated when the JVA was signed on Aug 16, 2016.

items.title: RM260mil UiTM funds channelled without MOF approval, PAC calls for stronger oversight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Almost RM260 million in funds channelled into Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Holdings entities and companies was not properly carried out as required under financial regulations and procedures, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) said. She said the findings were detailed in two PAC reports tabled in the Dewan Rakyat in 2024. "PAC also found critical structural weaknesses in the oversight and corporate governance of the institution's investment management.

items.title: Impact Capital moves closer to ACE Market listing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Impact Capital Holdings Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with Public Investment Bank Bhd (PIVB) ahead of its proposed listing on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market. The IPO will comprise a public issue of 96.69 million new shares and an offer for sale of 28.62 million existing shares in Impact Capital, an ICT systems integrator focused on critical infrastructure. Of the new shares, 24 million, or five per cent of the enlarged share capital, will be offered to Malaysian retail investors.

items.title: Dr Hasmah laid to rest at National Mausoleum as crowd of supporters gather in droves to pay last respects
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 28 — The remains of the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali have been laid to rest at the National Mausoleum in Precint 20, Putrajaya. The arrival was met by droves of supporters, as well as family and friends who gathered to pay their final respects. Crowds began gathering around the grave site as the remains, were lowered into the grave.

items.title: Police, RTD turn up heat on road hooligans in Iskandar Puteri
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Police seized 43 motorcycles and issued 112 summonses in an operation targeting illegal street racing and road hooliganism at the Lima Kedai toll plaza near here, yesterday The joint operation included federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department policemen and also state Road Transport Department officers. Acting district police chief Superintendent Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said 57 motorists, including five women, aged between 15 and 30, were inspected. Police issued 112 summonses, while RTD slapped offenders with106 notices for various offences, while 43 motorcycles were seized under Section 64 of the Road Transport Act 1987.

items.title: Poh Kong FY26 net profit jumps 60pct to RM193.37mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Poh Kong Holdings Bhd's net profit rose 59.7 per cent to RM193.37 million for the financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY26), from RM121.10 million a year earlier. For the fourth quarter (Q4), net profit rose to RM36.20 million from RM22.68 million in the corresponding quarter last year, while revenue increased to RM378.36 million from RM365.50 million. Poh Kong said revenue was largely derived from its retail segment.

items.title: Mukhriz asks public to forgive Siti Hasmah, settle any outstanding debts
items.summary: SERDANG: Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir today appealed to members of the public to forgive any wrongdoings or mistakes committed by his late mother, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, during her lifetime. He said the family would do its best to settle any debts left by Dr Siti Hasmah. Among those present were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail; former prime ministers Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob; and Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia ends marginally lower amid lack of fresh catalysts
items.summary: Turnover slipped to 3.11 billion units worth RM2.40 billion from 4.07 billion units valued at RM2.69 billion on Friday. In active trade, Zetrix AI was unchanged at 19 sen, Jaks Resources put on 1.5 sen to 18.5 sen, ACE Market debutant Evocom fell five sen to 13 sen, Aimax perked up half a sen to one sen, and Inari Amertron slid 11 sen to RM2.55. Warrants turnover trimmed to 944.79 million units worth RM156.45 million from 999.87 million units valued at RM180.99 million previously.

items.title: Azalina: Media freedom a key point in Freedom of Information Bill
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Media freedom is one of the key points in the proposed Freedom of Information (FOI) Bill 2026, says Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Azalina said this was in line with Article 10 of the Federal Constitution concerning freedom of speech. She said freedom of speech means little if the public and the media are denied basic access to accurate information.

items.title: Bank Negara: Malaysia’s financial markets remain orderly amid global headwinds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Malaysia’s domestic financial markets continued to adjust in an orderly manner, supported by balanced two-way flows that ensured effective price intermediation among market participants, according to Bank Negara Malaysia’s Financial Markets Committee (FMC). The FMC also said recent movements in the domestic financial markets were driven primarily by global factors, particularly developments in the US policy rate. This came amid a broader repricing of global interest rate expectations and higher global bond yields.

items.title: The wildfires choking Indonesia, sparking regional haze
items.summary: JAKARTA: For weeks, Indonesia has been battling fires that have burned vast swathes of forest and peat ecosystems, causing toxic haze to blanket parts of the country, Malaysia and Singapore. The fires have harmed humans and animals alike, and prompted criminal charges, licence suspensions and a presidentially mandated new agency to tackle fires in peat ecosystems. What is causing the fires?

items.title: From violin to rural medicine, 10 things Malaysians may have forgotten about Dr Hasmah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — It is easy to remember Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali through the people and institutions around her: as the wife of Malaysia’s longest-serving prime minister, as a former First Lady, or as the woman who stood beside Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad through decades of public life. As tributes pour in following her death at 100, here are 10 details that offer a glimpse of the Dr Hasmah that could have been missed by public eyes. Dr Hasmah recalled working with Unicef to train traditional midwives in cleaner and safer practices.

items.title: [UPDATED] Siti Hasmah laid to rest at Putrajaya National Cemetery [WATCH]
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The remains of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali were laid to rest at the Presint 20 Muslim Cemetery, Putrajaya, at 5.58pm today. Her husband, former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, and family members were present at the cemetery. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had earlier announced that Dr Siti Hasmah would be accorded a state funeral .

items.title: Penang governor, CM extend condolences over Siti Hasmah's passing
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Ramli Ngah Talib expressed deep grief over the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali. In a posting on his official social media page, Ramli and his wife, Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah, extended their heartfelt condolences to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his family. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow also extended his heartfelt condolences to the family of the late Dr Siti Hasmah.

items.title: Thai court dismisses petition challenging legality of 2026 election
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand's Constitutional Court on Monday dismissed a petition challenging the legality of February's general election, ruling that the ballot papers used did not violate voter secrecy. The court case stemmed from a petition filed by the ombudsman that argued that barcodes and QR (quick response) codes printed on ballot papers could be used to identify which candidate and party a voter chose. The Election Commission had said the codes were used for security purposes and that identifying a voter would require access to ballot stubs that were stored separately.

items.title: Over 2,000 gather to pay final respects to Siti Hasmah
items.summary: SERDANG: More than 2,000 congregants gathered at Masjid As Syarif, Taman Sungai Besi Indah this afternoon to perform funeral prayers for Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, arrived at about 4pm, while former prime ministers Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob were among other political leaders present. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan were also among those who paid their respects.

items.title: Hundreds gather at Seri Kembangan mosque to pay final respects to Dr Hasmah
items.summary: Her husband, former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, arrived in a separate vehicle travelling alongside the hearse carrying his wife’s remains. Former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad arrives at the As-Syarif Mosque in Seri Kembangan on September 28, 2026. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, arrived around 4pm to pay their respects to the bereaved family.

items.title: Malaysia's financial markets remain orderly amid global headwinds: Bank Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's domestic financial markets continued to adjust in an orderly manner, supported by balanced two-way flows that ensured effective price intermediation among market participants, according to Bank Negara Malaysia's Financial Markets Committee (FMC). The FMC also said recent movements in the domestic financial markets were driven primarily by global factors, particularly developments in the US policy rate. This came amid a broader repricing of global interest rate expectations and higher global bond yields.

items.title: [UPDATED] Siti Hasmah's remains leave mosque for burial at National Cemetery
items.summary: The remains were taken from the mosque following funeral prayers after Asar. More than 2,000 congregants gathered at the mosque for the funeral prayers for the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad. Among those present were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, who arrived about 4pm.

items.title: ERS Energy crosses 1.5GWh BESS milestone
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ERS Energy Sdn Bhd says it has surpassed 1.5 gigawatt-hours (GWh) in cumulative utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity across Southeast Asia. ERS Energy said the projects strengthen its expansion beyond solar engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning into utility-scale energy storage development and system integration. ERS Energy said it is pursuing further opportunities in Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam and Australia, where increasing renewable energy penetration is driving demand for grid flexibility and energy storage.

items.title: Fugro deploys autonomous underwater vehicle for Petronas ultra-deepwater survey
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Fugro has completed a geohazard site survey commissioned by Petronas Carigali Sdn Bhd for the Megah and Limbayong fields off Sabah, supporting the development of Malaysia's offshore resources. Fugro deployed its Echo Surveyor 8 AUV from the Fugro Equator to collect high-resolution bathymetric, geophysical and shallow subsurface data while operating close to the seabed. Fugro said the use of AUV technology and remote operations enabled faster data delivery and more efficient survey execution.

items.title: Released earlier this year, Federal Court now orders two men back to jail for cannabis trafficking
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 28 — Two men released from prison earlier this year must return to serve the remainder of their original 30-year sentence, after the Federal Court reinstated their convictions for trafficking 264.36 grammes of cannabis. “We find there was overwhelming evidence of trafficking as found by the trial court,” he said. The Federal Court reinstated the 30-year jail term that the High Court had imposed on both men on Oct 20, 2023.

items.title: Police freeze 5 bank accounts in Mandiri probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have frozen five bank accounts in connection with their investigation into Mandiri Development Centre Sdn Bhd (Mandiri), but have not disclosed the amount involved. Bukit Aman Anti-Money Laundering Criminal Investigation Unit chief Datuk Fazlisyam Abdul Majid said investigations were ongoing, with several more individuals to be called to have their statements recorded. "So far, five bank accounts belonging to parties under investigation have been frozen," he said when contacted today.

items.title: Siti Hasmah once dreamt of being a journalist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Long before she became known as the woman beside a prime minister, a young Hasmah Mohd Ali of Klang dreamt of becoming a journalist. But life took her down a different path, and the young lady who would eventually become known as Tun Dr Siti Hasmah would instead go on to make history herself. She died at the age of 100, leaving behind a legacy deeply rooted in Malaysias rural communities.

items.title: Former Negri exco members face more than 60 questions from Bukit Aman
items.summary: SEREMBAN: More than 60 questions were posed to 10 former Negri Sembilan executive councilors today as Bukit Aman recorded their statements over the state's constitutional crisis. Former state Industry, Technology, Innovation and Digital exco Datuk Mohd Asna Amin said the questions focused mainly on the ongoing crisis, with each exco member's statement recorded separately in sessions lasting between 30 and 35 minutes. "The Negri Sembilan State Constitution 1959 (UUTKNS) serves as the guide.

items.title: JPJ cracks down on foreign drivers, 481,119 summonses issued from 2024 to Sept 2026
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 28 — A total of 481,119 summonses were issued by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) against foreign drivers through the special operation codenamed ‘Ops Khas Pemandu Warga Asing’ (PeWA) from 2024 to September this year. JPJ senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the main offences detected were not possessing a Competent Driving Licence, expired Motor Vehicle Licence and no insurance coverage. He said that foreigners are not allowed to apply for vocational licences such as Goods Vehicle Licence and Public Service Vehicle Licence, therefore employers need to ensure that lorry or bus drivers meet all the stipulated requirements.

items.title: Rapid KL vows cooperation in probe of bus crash that killed foreign student
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA: Rapid KL has confirmed that one of its buses was involved in a crash along Persiaran Subang Permai here that killed a 19-year-old foreign student this morning. It said the bus, operating on route T776 (USJ 7 Station-Subang Mewah), was travelling towards Subang Mewah at 6.19am when it collided with several vehicles parked on the road shoulder. "A motorcycle at the location was also involved in the incident, leaving its rider and pillion rider injured.

items.title: Civil servant, ex‑CEO plead not guilty to RM18,000 gold mining graft charges
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 28 — A civil servant and a former chief executive officer today pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here to three corruption charges involving RM18,000 in bribes allegedly linked to facilitating gold mining operations in Sabah. According to the charges, Chong allegedly gave Robert cash loans of RM10,000 in April 2024, RM3,000 in October 2024 and RM5,000 in October 2025 as an inducement to facilitate the company’s gold mining operations. Robert was separately charged under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009 with corruptly obtaining the three cash loans from Chong to facilitate the company’s gold mining operations, with the same penalties under Section 24(1).

items.title: Fahmi tells telcos: Rethink diesel gensets, embrace renewables for tower operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The government has called on telecommunications companies to reassess their reliance on diesel generator sets (gensets) to operate some 60,000 telecommunication towers nationwide, particularly in rural areas. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the large-scale use of fossil fuels to keep telecommunication towers operational needed to be gradually reduced by switching to renewable energy sources, in line with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR). “There are about 60,000 telecommunication towers nationwide.

items.title: India's top court says need to fix accountability over Delhi rape cases
items.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court of India on Monday pushed for accountability over a recent spate of rape cases in the national capital and neighbouring districts, saying they reflected a "failure of law enforcement", local media reported. The Supreme Court said public spaces, including parks and buses, could not become "high-risk" zones because of poor lighting and surveillance, and other basic facilities, legal news website Live Law reported. The court said fixing accountability was necessary and directed its administration to file a public interest petition on the issue for the court to pursue, legal news website Bar and Bench said.

items.title: Sabah police say gospel singer Israel Houghton concert unsuitable now, two reports lodged
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 28 — Sabah police will advise the state government to postpone American gospel singer Israel Houghton’s concert if a formal application is submitted. Sabah police commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun said the stance takes into account public reaction and community sensitivities about the concert at this time. He said police have so far received two reports concerning the event and will continue to monitor the situation, including obtaining statements from relevant parties.

items.title: Foreign student killed as bus crashes into four vehicles in Subang Jaya
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA: A 19-year-old foreign student was killed after a bus crashed into four other vehicles at Jalan USJ 1 here this morning. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said the bus, driven by a 29-year-old man, was travelling from Persiaran Subang Mewah towards Edumetro when the driver is believed to have lost control of the vehicle. "The pillion rider was pronounced dead at the scene, while the motorcycle rider suffered serious injuries and was taken to Shah Alam Hospital for treatment," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Crowds gather at mosque for Siti Hasmah's funeral prayers
items.summary: SERDANG: A sombre atmosphere prevailed at Masjid As Syarif, Taman Sungai Besi Indah, this afternoon as political leaders, senior government officials, prominent figures and members of the public gathered to pay their final respects to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali. Members of the public began arriving at the mosque as early as 1pm, ahead of the funeral prayers for the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad. Among those seen at the mosque were former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Royal Malaysian Navy chief Admiral Tan Sri Zulhelmy Ithnain and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.

items.title: Singapore-registered Audi investigated for dangerous driving on NSE
items.summary: MUAR: Police are investigating two drivers, including the driver of a Singapore-registered Audi, for flashing strobe lights and driving dangerously on the North-South Expressway near yesterday. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said investigations revealed that the incident occurred at 5.48am yesterday at Km135 (southbound). He said after the footage went viral, police lodged a first information report with its traffic division.

items.title: Malaysia’s passport now No. 2 globally, sharing silver tier with Singapore
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 28 — The Malaysian passport is now ranked second globally in The Passport Index Global Ranking 2026, rising from third last year. “Based on the ranking, Malaysian passport holders have access to 175 destinations, comprising 129 visa-free destinations and 46 destinations with visa-on-arrival, while 23 destinations require a visa,” according to the post. Based on data from www.passportindex.org, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) passport holds the top spot in the Passport Power Rank, followed by Singapore and Malaysia in second place.

items.title: Lee Chong Wei mourns Dr Hasmah: ‘To us, she was a warrior’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Badminton legend Datuk Seri Lee Chong Wei has paid tribute to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, remembering her as a “warrior” and a source of affection for the national squad, following her death today at the age of 100. Lee said her love for badminton “never faded”, and that he had not realised it would be their last conversation. But to me and the entire national badminton squad, Tun was a warrior, the person we respected most,” he said.

items.title: Singapore Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong recalls Dr Hasmah’s humour, zest and love for music
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Sept 28 — The late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah was a warm and gracious person, full of life, and had a wonderful sense of humour, said Singapore Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong. Dr Siti Hasmah, wife of former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, passed away at the National Heart Institute (IJN), Kuala Lumpur on Monday morning at the age of 100. “Ho Ching and I will remember Tun Siti Hasmah fondly,” he said in his Facebook post on Monday.

items.title: HEAL 15555 crisis line records 267,873 calls for counselling, intervention since Covid‑19 pandemic
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 28 — The National Mental Health Crisis Line (HEAL 15555) has intervened in 518 behavioural crisis cases over the past four years, covering suicidal ideation and suicide attempts. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said that of that figure, 347 cases were of suicidal ideation. He said of that total, 220,856 clients (82 per cent) received emotional support assistance, while 47,014 clients (18 per cent) received specific intervention by counselling psychology officers.

items.title: Religious teacher pleads not guilty to sexual assault charges involving 16‑year‑old boy in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 28 — A religious teacher, known as an ustazah, at a national secondary school was charged at the Sessions Court here today with three counts of physical sexual assault against a 16-year-old male student two years ago. The accused, Haslina Abu Bakar, 48, however, pleaded not guilty to all charges read before Judge Ainul Sharin Mohamad. According to the first charge, the accused is alleged to have committed physical sexual assault by kissing the boy on the mouth for sexual purposes in November 2024.

items.title: Fahmi: Dr Hasmah to be laid to rest beside Endon Mahmood at National Mausoleum
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The remains of the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali will be laid to rest beside the tomb of Tun Endon Mahmood, the late wife of Malaysia's fifth prime minister Tun Abdullah Ahmad Badawi. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil disclosed this while sharing the funeral arrangements, after paying his respects at Dr Hasmah's family residence in Seri Kembangan earlier this afternoon. “My wife told me that she (Dr Siti Hasmah) spoke a lot about God.

items.title: Tabung Haji opens Haj appeals Oct 2, earlier start gives pilgrims more prep time
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Tabung Haji (TH) will open appeals for the 1448H/2027 Haj season via the THiJARI application and website from Oct 2, a month earlier than in the previous season. TH Group managing director and chief executive officer Mustakim Mohamad said the earlier opening would give prospective pilgrims more time to prepare financially, physically and in terms of their knowledge of the Haj. “The Haj payment for pilgrims selected through the appeal process is the full Haj cost of RM33,300 for the 1448H/2027 season, in line with the concept of istito’ah in fulfilling the obligation to perform the Haj.

items.title: Elderly woman found stabbed to death in Menglembu, daughter with psychiatric history held
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 70-year-old victim was found with a stab wound to her chest and was believed to have been killed by her daughter, who has a history of mental health treatment. He said police received a report from the victim’s son-in-law at about 7pm. Mohd Alwi said police also seized a knife believed to have been used in the incident.

items.title: Major city roads, highways to close this weekend for KL Marathon 2026
items.summary: They include Jalan Raja, Jalan Raja Laut, Jalan Dang Wangi, Jalan Munshi Abdullah, Jalan Ampang, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan P. Ramlee, Jalan Raja Chulan, Jalan Kuching, Jalan Kinabalu and Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin. From 11.00pm on Saturday, Jalan TAR, Jalan Tun Perak, the AKLEH, MRR2 and the northbound DUKE Highway towards Jalan Duta will also shut. Jalan Sultan Ismail is expected to reopen at 6.30am, Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman at 9.00am, and Jalan Tun Perak and Jalan Dang Wangi at 9.30am.

items.title: Azalina: Freedom of Information Bill must balance openness with safeguards, avoid excessive prohibitions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The proposed Freedom of Information Bill 2026 must genuinely provide access to information and should not impose excessive restrictions that undermine the purpose of the legislation, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. “You must make sure that if you have the FOI (Freedom of Information Act), it must be for information. She said the session also enabled the JKPK to hear views from the public, including the younger generation, while helping the committee review weaknesses identified in the existing blue bill.

items.title: Thunderstorm warning in effect for Pahang, Sarawak and Sabah until 5pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for parts of Pahang, Sarawak, and Sabah, with heavy rain, gusty winds, and lightning expected to persist until 5pm today. In Sarawak, the alert covers the Bintulu division (Bintulu and Sebauh), Miri, and the Limbang division. In Sabah, the warning covers a wider area, encompassing Tawau, the Sandakan division (Tongod, Telupid, Kinabatangan, and Sandakan), the Interior division (Sook, Keningau, Tambunan, Membakut, and Pensiangan), alongside the West Coast division and Kudat.

items.title: Mourners gather to pay last respects to Dr Hasmah at Seri Kembangan home
items.summary: SERDANG, Sept 28 — A quiet but steady stream of mourners arrived at the Seri Kembangan residence of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad to pay their last respects to his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, who died earlier today. Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad performs prayers with family and friends as they pay their last respects to the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali at their residence at The Mines Residence, Sungai Besi, September 28, 2026. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil were also among those who arrived to offer prayers and condolences.

items.title: Rosmah faces Mareva injunction bid, 1MDB seeks to freeze US$346m luxury assets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The High Court here has fixed Jan 7 next year to hear the Mareva injunction application filed by 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and 10 other companies against Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor. On May 9, 2024, 1MDB and the 10 companies, including five of its subsidiaries, namely 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited, 1MDB Energy Limited, 1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited, Global Diversified Investment Company Limited and SRC International Sdn Bhd filed the lawsuit against Rosmah. The other plaintiffs are Affinity Equity International Partners Limited, Alsen Chance Holdings Limited, BlackRock Commodities (Global) Limited, Blackstone Asia Real Estate Partners Limited and Brightstone Jewellery Limited.

items.title: Roti canai maker charged in Kota Tinggi court with murder of five‑year‑old niece at Tanjung Sedili river
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 28 — A roti canai maker was charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of his five-year-old niece in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili, here last week. No plea was recorded from Abadi Mohd Yasro, 37, after the charge was read out before Magistrate Nur Najihah Hamidi, as the case is triable by the High Court. According to the charge sheet, the father of three allegedly murdered Putri Nur Affiya Qhalhesya Shahrul, five, at about 8.20am on Sept 21 at a river in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili, Kota Tinggi.

items.title: Economy Minister Akmal says RM2,000 minimum wage decision rests with PM Anwar in Budget 2027
items.summary: He also said that the Federal Government had allocated RM127 million under Rolling Plan 1 (RP1) of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) for the repair and maintenance of police quarters and stations nationwide. Akmal Nasrullah said the allocation included an additional RM5 million through a Notice of Change (NOC), bringing the total allocation to RM127 million from the original RM122 million. Of the total, RM44.35 million was allocated for the repair and maintenance of police stations, while RM77.65 million was for the repair and maintenance of 3,716 quarters nationwide.

items.title: Wan Junaidi, Hajiji extend condolences to Dr Mahathir over Dr Hasmah’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Leaders in Sabah and Sarawak have extended their condolences to former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his family following the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, today. In Kuching, Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar and his wife, Toh Puan Fauziah Mohd Sanusi, paid tribute to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah’s contributions to medicine and public health. In Kota Kinabalu, Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor described Tun Dr Siti Hasmah’s death as a profound loss felt not only by Dr Mahathir and their family but by Malaysians across the country.

items.title: Dr Hasmah was ‘mother figure’ to 1992 Thomas Cup squad, says Razif Sidek
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — National badminton legend Datuk Razif Sidek described the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali as a great loss to the Malaysian badminton family, particularly the members of the 1992 Thomas Cup squad who ended the country’s 25-year wait for the prestigious trophy 34 years ago. He said Tun Dr Siti Hasmah’s presence in Barcelona was particularly meaningful to the national badminton players, especially for the support and encouragement she provided throughout the Games. “Alhamdulillah, we managed to bring home the country’s first Olympic medal at the time,” said Razif, who last met Tun Dr Siti Hasmah last year.

items.title: Police maintain 24‑hour presence at Najib’s Langgak Duta home pending further instructions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Security at the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak in Jalan Langgak Duta here is still being maintained around the clock, said Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus. He was speaking after attending the handover ceremony for the Kuala Lumpur Special Branch chief and Dang Wangi district police chief at the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters (IPK) today. Fadil said the security detail at the residence involves personnel from the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) and the Kuala Lumpur IPK.

items.title: N. Sembilan royal crisis: Former exco members arrive at MAINS Tower to give statements to Bukit Aman team
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 28 — Several former Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (Exco) members have arrived at the Negeri Sembilan Islamic Religious Council (MAINS) Tower here to have their statements recorded by a Bukit Aman team, following the current crisis in the state. Among the former Exco members are Datuk Faizal Ramli, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siti Nur Umaira binti Hasim, Suhaimizan Bizar, and Datuk Razali Abu Samah; they arrived separately starting at 10am today. It is understood that police personnel and officers have also arrived at the tower to record the statements of the former Exco members.

items.title: Zahid: Dr Hasmah’s death a profound loss to nation, family
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi described the passing of the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali as a profound loss for the nation and, in particular, for her family. Ahmad Zahid said Tun Dr Siti Hasmah is also remembered for her service as a doctor and her concern for the well-being of the community, indeed, her personality, gentleness, humility, and steadfastness throughout her life made her a beloved figure and a role model for Malaysians. “This morning, the nation mourns the passing of the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah, a highly respected woman who held a special place in the hearts of Malaysians.
